newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Volcan may seek partner for Mahr Tunel.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Volcan may seek partner for Mahr Tunel.

text.p: Peruvian miner Volcan, whose purchase of the state-owned Mahr Tunel mining unit Friday sent its shares up 10.01 percent to 16.49 soles, said it might start looking for a partnership with a foreign company.
"We are holding discussions, and approaching (other mining companies) but for the moment there is nothing decisive," said Eduardo Llosa, general manager of Volcan, after Friday's sale.
Volcan, by bidding $127 million and promising a minimum investment of $60 million over the next five years, was the winner Friday of the auction for the Mahr Tunel privatization.
Market sources said they believed the call for a partnership was a sign the company might not be able to pay what it has promised.

"It's a lot of money and Volcan does not have enough capital to sustain the investment," said Manuel Torres from Finvest brokerage. "Volcan must find an association to maintain its investment in the Mahr Tunel."
However, Llosa said that Volcan had its finances secured and that Fleming bank had assisted them during the transaction.
"Our finances are assured, and Fleming bank was our advisor," said Llorca. "If we have paid this sum, it is because we know ... the price for Mahr Tunel."
The Mahr Tunel SA unit controls the San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines, which are neighbors in the central Peruvian highlands.
Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver, while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc.
